missing_spec_content.spec_text: Required practical activity 1: investigation to determine the specific heat capacity of one or more materials. The investigation will involve linking the decrease of one energy store (or work done) to the increase in temperature and subsequent increase in thermal energy stored.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson teaches only the equation ΔE = mcΔθ. It never describes the required practical: the method, what is measured, or how the decrease in one energy store (or work done) is linked to the temperature rise to find c.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: AT 1 Investigate the transfer of energy from a gravitational potential energy store to a kinetic energy store.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson treats GPE to KE only as a calculation (mgh = ½mv²). It gives no practical or investigative context. This is listed as a key opportunity rather than core content, so it is a lower-priority gap.

factual_errors.text: Specific heat capacity is in this topic too. It tells you how much energy is needed to heat something up.
factual_errors.correction: Specific heat capacity is the energy needed to raise the temperature of one kilogram of a substance by one degree Celsius. The total energy needed to heat an object is the change in thermal energy, ΔE, not c.

factual_errors.text: Specific heat capacity — how much energy to heat something
factual_errors.correction: Specific heat capacity is the energy per kilogram per degree Celsius ('the amount of energy required to raise the temperature of one kilogram of the substance by one degree Celsius'). It is not the total energy needed to heat an object.

wrong_terms.text: All the GPE at the top converts to KE at the bottom
wrong_terms.spec_term: transfer of energy from a gravitational potential energy store to a kinetic energy store

wrong_terms.text: Falling object (no air resistance): GPE at top converts to KE at bottom
wrong_terms.spec_term: transfer of energy from a gravitational potential energy store to a kinetic energy store
